'''Kal Brigger''' was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] freelance [[Merchant/Legends|trader]] who, along with his sister, [[Dova Brigger]], bought the [[YT-1300 light freighter/Legends|YT-1300 light freighter]] [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']], known at the [[Time/Legends|time]] as YT 492727ZED, in [[48 BBY/Legends|48 BBY]]. Using their newly bought [[Starship/Legends|ship]], which they named ''Hardwired'', the siblings [[Smuggler/Legends|illegally transported]] cargo between [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]] and other [[Planet/Legends|planets]] in the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]]. Eventually, the Briggers became involved with the [[Smugglers' Confederation]] and its leader, [[Nirama]], who put a [[Bounty/Legends|price]] on the siblings' heads due to a broken deal in which Kal was supposed to stop his dealings with [[Slavery/Legends|slavers]]. After a [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] captured Dova, Kal took the ''Hardwired'' for himself and rechristened the ship as ''Wayward Son''. Kal then went to work for the former smuggler [[Iaco Stark/Legends|Iaco Stark]], who had gotten into an armed [[Stark Hyperspace War/Legends|conflict]] with the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], during which Kal was [[Death/Legends|eaten alive]] by [[Diet/Legends|carnivorous]] [[Challat eater|insects]] in an abandoned [[Spice/Legends|spice]] [[Mining/Legends|mine]] on [[Troiken/Legends|Troiken]].

==Biography==
===Life===
Kal Brigger and his sister, [[Dova Brigger|Dova]], a pair of freelance [[Merchant/Legends|traders]], worked in the enterprising business during their careers. In [[48 BBY/Legends|48 BBY]], the Briggers came across a [[YT-1300 light freighter/Legends|YT-1300 light freighter]], owned by [[Corell Industries Limited/Legends|Corell Industries]], which had gone bankrupt due to the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]], who had been monopolizing various businesses. The siblings bought the [[Starship/Legends|ship]] and named it [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Hardwired'']], with the intent of making a profit by [[Smuggler/Legends|transporting]] cargo between [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]] and other [[Planet/Legends|worlds]]. Successful in his business, Kal used the money they made toward upgrading the ship's [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]], hoping for easier travel in the [[Corellian system/Legends|Corellian system]], and eventually used the hyperdrive to enable travel to other [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]].<ref name="Millennium Falcon" />

However, the Briggers' business soon turned illegal, and they began to carry different cargo, including munitions, light arms, and [[Slavery/Legends|slaves]] instead of consumer goods. This illegal business caught the attention of the [[Smugglers' Confederation|Smugglers' Confederacy]] of the [[Cularin system/Legends|Cularin system]] and their leader, [[Nirama]]. An [[Oblee]] [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord]] opposed to slavery, Nirama struck a deal with Kal hoping the Briggers would stop business with slavers. If they complied, Nirama would loan them [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] to upgrade the ''Hardwired'' in return.<ref name="Millennium Falcon" />

After a standard year, though, Kal and Dova broke the deal, prompting Nirama to put a [[Bounty/Legends|price]] on their heads. A famed [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] succeeded in capturing Dova, who in turn was executed by Nirama, though Kal escaped. Alone, Kal rechristened the ''Hardwired'' as ''Wayward Son'', and attempted to take a job with [[Iaco Stark/Legends|Iaco Stark's]] [[Stark Commercial Combine|Commercial Combine]]. This involvement with Stark, a former smuggler who headed a group of [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]], bounty hunters, and [[Assassin/Legends|assassins]], backfired on Kal when Stark became involved in an armed [[Stark Hyperspace War/Legends|conflict]] with the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] because of stolen [[Bacta/Legends|bacta]]. The Republic forces released [[Diet/Legends|carnivorous]] insects against the smuggler on [[Troiken/Legends|Troiken]], and Kal was eaten alive by them, trapped in an abandoned [[Spice/Legends|spice]] [[Mining/Legends|mine]].<ref name="Millennium Falcon" />

===Legacy===
Brigger's ship, the ''Wayward Son'', would pass down through many owners, including [[Tobb Jadak]], a member of the clandestine [[Republic Group/Legends|Republic Group]]; [[Bammy Decree/Legends|Bammy Decree]], a [[Technician/Legends|mechanic]], who, in dating the history of the ship, chronicled Brigger's ownership of it until he had been killed; and eventually [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]] and [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]], [[Heroes of Yavin/Legends|heroes]] of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]], with whom the ship became famous under the name the ''Millennium Falcon''.<ref name="Millennium Falcon" />

==Personality and traits==
Kal Brigger was a trader in the enterprising business, whose dealings soon turned illegal after he began to make a profit from his criminal activities. Brigger also broke a deal with Nirama, leading the crime lord to place a bounty on his head due to his dealings with slavers.<ref name="Millennium Falcon" />

==Behind the scenes==
The character of Kal Brigger was first mentioned in [[Millennium Falcon (novel)|''Millennium Falcon'']], a [[2008]] novel that was written by [[James Luceno]]. He later received a further mention in the reference book ''[[Millennium Falcon Owner's Workshop Manual]]''.
